title.justification: The paper focuses on methods to enhance code performance by using machine learning to provide prescriptive feedback to programmers.
title.quote: L EARNING TO I MPROVE C ODE E FFICIENCY

extractions.description: The paper proposes utilizing machine learning to provide prescriptive feedback to software developers to enhance code efficiency. It analyzes competitive programming datasets to understand code efficiency variations and suggests using a discrete variational auto-encoder model to provide code-edit hints that improve performance. This approach could potentially help in reducing computational costs and carbon footprint by promoting high-performance code development.

climate_change_is_central.justification: The paper explicitly mentions the importance of efficient coding practices not only for performance improvements but also for reducing the carbon footprint of computing, linking it directly to concerns of environmental impact.
climate_change_is_central.quote: As these automatic performance increases slow down, the burden of reducing computational cost and carbon footprint now falls on writing high-performance code (Patterson et al. (2021)).

secondary_categories.justification: By optimizing code efficiency and reducing the carbon footprint, the paper also touches upon managing pollution, particularly in terms of emissions from data centers.
secondary_categories.quote: As we move towards building more ML models that can write code, it is critical that we also consider computational efficiency. Code that is run in datacenters across the world today contributes to not only cost, but also the carbon footprint of machines.
